record.title: Firebase functions env files and runtimeconfig hold NILE_API_KEY values in the source tree
record.description: The files .env.nile-production, .env.nile-staging and .runtimeconfig.json in backend/functions/firebase/functions each hold a NILE-API-KEY credential (key names NILE_API_KEY and nile_api.key; values not reproduced here). The only ignore file on the path, functions/.gitignore, lists only 'lib', and the repo root .gitignore has no .env* or .runtimeconfig.json rule. The Sapling treestate (.sl/treestate) records all three file names, so they are very likely tracked. The only in-repo consumer, priceMailer.ts, is commented out of index.ts. No code under backend/ validates the NILE-API-KEY header or serves the Jobs/sendPriceMailer endpoint it calls, so what the key authenticates to, and whether it is live, cannot be established from this scope.
record.claimed_root_cause: Environment secrets for a server-to-server call (NILE-API-KEY header to the API Jobs/sendPriceMailer endpoint) are stored as plaintext files in the repository working tree and are not excluded by any ignore rule, rather than being held in Secret Manager or a git-ignored local file.

trace.scope: dotenv file for the nile-production Firebase functions deployment
trace.description: Plaintext NILE_API_KEY next to NILE_API_URL pointing at the production API host. Readable by anyone with repository access.
NILE_API_KEY is read from process.env, which Firebase populates from the .env.<project> file at deploy time.
The key is sent as the NILE-API-KEY header on PUT Jobs/sendPriceMailer. All exports are commented out in src/index.ts lines 8 and 15-17, so this is currently not deployed from this source.

evidence.description: Legacy runtime config nile_api.key credentials in plaintext; lines 3-4 hold values.
Contains only 'lib'; none of the three secret files is ignored.
priceMailer import and exports are commented out (lines 8 and 15-17), so the consumer is disabled.
Root .gitignore (core/.gitignore) ignores .firebaserc, .firebaseConfig.json and .firebase, but has no .env* or .runtimeconfig.json pattern.

blockers: Sapling tracking is only inferred: .sl/treestate lists the three filenames, but whether they are committed in history (or only present in the working copy) was not confirmed without running sl.
The receiving API (Jobs/sendPriceMailer, NILE-API-KEY validation) is not in backend/ scope, so the key's privileges and whether it is currently valid or rotated cannot be determined from source.
The only consumer function is disabled, which lowers the likelihood that the key is still active.

validation_plan.local: Repository owner runs 'sl files' or 'sl log -f' on the three paths to confirm they are tracked and in how many commits, and checks who can read the repo.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks whether the production and staging NILE_API_KEY values are still accepted by the API (via the key store or audit logs, not a live probe). If active, rotate them, move them to Secret Manager or a git-ignored file, add .env.* and .runtimeconfig.json to .gitignore, and purge them from history.
